home_trend_title: What the Bonito Bonito baby dance is, move by move
home_trend_lead: Bonito, bonito is Spanish for “nice, nice”, sung in diminutives: un cafecito (a little coffee), riquito (so tasty), una sonrisita (a little smile). The Bonito Bonito baby dance is that list turned into hands, in the song's order — bonito, bonito, un cafecito, riquito, riquito, una sonrisita — so every move you see matches a line you hear. One gesture per line, looped, which is why an eight-second cut already reads as a whole dance.
home_trend_move_1_text: Both hands up, then out. The hook, and the frame everyone screenshots.
home_trend_move_2_text: Mime a sip. This is the move people mean when they search for the cafecito baby dance.
home_trend_move_3_text: Rub the belly in circles, twice, on the beat.
home_trend_move_4_text: One finger under the chin. The smile cue, and the second most of these videos get cut at.
home_trend_note: The 12-second version adds the wave at the start and the sway at the end, so it plays as a routine rather than four separate clips.
